request: Client participants: let a client contact hold a principal in an organization and take part in requests raised for their client — sign in, be the addressee of a request, answer or decline it — without becoming a member of staff.

findings.claim: An account can hold a row in both membership tables at once, so a reachable state matches two rows of REQ-02-002's decision table with incompatible outcomes: create a second ClientMembership, or restore the existing one.

witness.detail: REQ-02-002 (:82) 're-read both membership tables inside the accept transaction and decide by the row found'. Row (:91): '| removedMembership | The `ClientMembership` is created `active`; the removed staff row is untouched. |' Row (:93): '| removedClientMembershipBoundClient | That row is restored …; no second row is created. |' The domain is declared single-valued (:85 'domains=(heldRow: none|activeMembership|removedMembership|…)'), but `accountId` is unique per table, not across them — 02-client-participants.contracts.md:100 '| `accountId` | `String` `@unique` FK → `Account` …' for ClientMembership, and apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:191 'accountId String @unique' for Membership — so one account can hold a removed Membership AND a removed ClientMembership at the same time. That state is reached entirely by this spec's own rules: :91 creates a ClientMembership for an account holding a removed Membership and leaves the staff row untouched, then REQ-02-028 (:277) removes the client row. A client invitation for the bound client then matches both :91 (create — which the Decided note at :101 says `accountId @unique` turns into a 500) and :93 (restore). The State Machine (:436) answers only the second: '| removed | acceptInviteForBoundClient | The row is restored to `active` (REQ-02-023). |'

findings.suggestedFix: State the order the two tables are consulted in — read the ClientMembership first and decide on it, and only when there is none decide on the Membership row — and re-key the decision table so no reachable state matches two rows.

findings.claim: Reassigning a request to a client user is governed by two refusals the reassign route is declared unable to give, so a reassignment to a client user of another client, or of a request that carries no project, has two mutually exclusive answers.

witness.detail: REQ-02-034 (:315) is unscoped: 'IF the project's `clientId` differs from the addressee's `clientId`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer `400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.contactProjectMismatch`.' REQ-02-033 (:310) likewise: 'IF a request addressed to a client user carries no `projectId`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer `400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.projectRequiredForClient`.' Both sit under '### Addressing a request to a client user', and REQ-02-053 (:412) confirms that section covers reassignment: 'WHEN a request is addressed to a client user by creation or by reassignment…'. But 02-client-participants.contracts.md:26 declares the reassign route's whole error set as '`403 TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden`; `400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.clientUserUnavailable`', and contracts:71-72 bind both messages to one route only: '| `REQUEST_MESSAGES.projectRequiredForClient` | `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests` | …' and '| `REQUEST_MESSAGES.contactProjectMismatch` | `POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests` | …'. contracts:1-3 makes the disagreement fatal rather than cosmetic: 'a status a case expects and this file does not declare is a lint error'. Both states are reachable — a member-to-member request with no `projectId` (schema.prisma:1145 'projectId String?') reassigned to a client user, and a reassignment naming a client user of another client. No implementation answers REQ-02-033/034 and stays inside the declared error set.

findings.suggestedFix: Decide one answer for each case on reassignment and state it in both places — either add `400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.projectRequiredForClient` and `400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.contactProjectMismatch` to the reassign route row and to their Error Messages rows, or scope REQ-02-033 and REQ-02-034 to creation and say what reassignment answers instead.

findings.claim: The declared `GET /api/me` body for a client principal carries an `account` object the endpoint does not produce and the app shell cannot render — `displayName` instead of `firstName`/`lastName` — so a client principal signing in reaches a shell that throws instead of a screen.

witness.detail: The spec declares (02-client-participants.contracts.md:40): '{ "account": { "id": "…", "displayName": "J. Client", "email": "j.client@acme.example" },' and REQ-02-014 (:185) governs that route. What the route returns today — `grep -n 'firstName\|lastName\|displayName' apps/api/src/members/me.controller.ts` → '32:        firstName: membership.account.firstName,' '33:        lastName: membership.account.lastName,' and no `displayName` anywhere in the body. What consumes it — `grep -n 'firstName' apps/web/src/layout/Topbar.tsx` → '36:  const name = `${account.firstName} ${account.lastName}`;' '37:  const initials = `${account.firstName.charAt(0)}${account.lastName.charAt(0)}`.toUpperCase();', reached for every signed-in screen through apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/layout.tsx:34 which resolves `/api/me` and hands the body straight to the shell (session-context.tsx:5-13 types `account` as `{ id, email, firstName, lastName, timezone, firstDayOfWeek }`). The same spec draws that name: the client inbox mock (contracts:190) shows 'J. Client ▾' in the top bar. An account object of `{ id, displayName, email }` makes `account.firstName.charAt(0)` throw, and Account has no `displayName` column (schema.prisma:33-34 'firstName String' / 'lastName String').

findings.suggestedFix: State the client body with the account fields the endpoint returns and the shell reads (`id`, `email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `timezone`, `firstDayOfWeek`) plus `principalKind` and `role: null`, or state that the account object becomes `displayName`-shaped for every principal and say what the top bar renders from.

findings.claim: REQ-02-052 does not say whether the request-detail *response* withholds the event trail from a client principal or only the screen omits the panel, and the two readings differ by whether a client can read the staff history over the API.

witness.detail: REQ-02-052 (:407): 'WHERE the viewer is a client principal, THE SYSTEM SHALL omit the History panel and every control they cannot use from the request detail.' Inputs: a client principal calls `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId}` for a request addressed to them, which has been reassigned once and had its priority changed. Reading A — 'the request detail' is the response (02-client-participants.contracts.md:22 declares that route): `events` comes back empty, and the client sees no trail. Reading B — 'the request detail' is the screen (the UI Description row at contracts:240, 'Client user, request detail | No History panel'): the response still carries every `RequestEvent` with `oldLabel`/`newLabel` display-name snapshots of staff (apps/api/src/requests/requests.dto.ts:60-70, `RequestEventDto` inside `RequestDetailDto`) and only the DOM omits the panel. Both satisfy the text; they differ in whether a client outside the organization's staff can read the internal trail. No case decides it: TC-02-E2E-03 asserts only `request-detail-history` absent from the DOM, and no integration case asserts the detail body for a client principal.

findings.suggestedFix: Say which fields `GET …/requests/{requestId}` returns to a client principal — name `events` as omitted or returned — and give the decision an integration case.

findings.claim: TC-02-INT-02's Expected Result closes with 'No `Invitation` row is written in any of the six' (02-client-participants.cases.md:65), but its Steps list seven bodies — four as an admin and three as a `user` — and all seven are refusals.
findings.suggestedFix: Say seven, or drop the count and write 'in any of them'.

findings.claim: 'The client's copy of the four client-side rules is a convenience; the server re-validates all six' (02-client-participants.contracts.md:143) counts four client-side rules, but the table marks Server-only 'yes' on rules 3, 5 and 6, leaving three.
findings.suggestedFix: Say three, or drop the number.

findings.claim: The decision-table row sends the reader to the wrong requirement for the restore: '| removedClientMembershipBoundClient | That row is restored (REQ-02-022); no second row is created. |' — REQ-02-022 (:235) is the archived-client refusal; the restore is REQ-02-023 (:240), as the State Machine (:436) and REQ-02-023's own text say.
findings.suggestedFix: Point at REQ-02-023, or state the restore inline and drop the pointer.

findings.claim: No rule says removal writes `removedAt` and `removedByAccountId`. REQ-02-028 (:277) writes only `status` and the security stamp, while REQ-02-023 (:241) clears both columns on a restore and the data model (contracts:106-107) describes them as 'Cleared by a restore'. An implementation that never fills them passes TC-02-INT-21, which asserts only that they are 'unchanged from after the first' call, so the removal audit is silently empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the two writes to REQ-02-028 — `removedAt` the removal time and `removedByAccountId` the caller's account — and assert them in TC-02-INT-21.

findings.claim: Neither bundle file carries a `## Verification Plan`, which the spec template requires of every spec (.claude/skills/spec/references/spec-template.md:141) — the rig, the route to each state a case needs, and what was observed at spec time. Without it there is no record that the surface this hangs off was walked before the cases were written.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the section, or state in one line why nothing could be walked and give it a Known Gaps row.

findings.claim: The new client-user routes refuse an unentitled staff caller with `403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.manageForbidden`, where every sibling route under the same `/clients/{clientId}` prefix answers 404 for a caller lacking the client capability — apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts:368-372, 'A missing capability collapses to 404 rather than 403 — mirroring `OrgScopeGuard`'. So a `user` who opens a client detail is told it does not exist and, on the People sub-resource of the same client, is told they lack a permission. Recorded so a person can confirm the difference was meant.
